# Balanced forces, steady motion

<!-- STEP id="box" -->
A person pushes a moving box forward with a force equal to the friction on it. The two forces are equal and opposite, so the net force is zero. By the first law, the box keeps moving with a constant velocity.

<!-- STEP id="add" -->
In the real world, some force always acts on an object. But we can add forces so that the net force becomes zero. A weightlifter holding a barbell steady is one example. A push that balances friction is another.
